items.title: They Accused Him of Lying About AI
items.summary: This one stuck with me. The writer was a regional winner of the 2026 Commonwealth Short Story Prize. The Commonwealth Foundation read the winners' drafts and notes and says it's satisfied AI wasn't used. Pangram says its false alarm rate is extremely low, but the Authors Guild says there's no truly reliable test for AI. Most of us will never get a review like that. If you make things for a living, your drafts may be your best proof. Do you save yours?

items.title: Making AI Agents Agree Before Work Starts
items.summary: In episode 1041 of the SuperDataScience podcast, Jon Krohn discusses with Dr. Vijoy Pandey, SVP/GM Outshift by Cisco, how to ensure AI agents stay aligned and on task. Dr. Pandey explains the concept of a protocol layer, similar to a car's lane correction, to prevent intent drift in multi-agent systems. He describes a protocol, ACCORD, that creates a shared, locked contract for agent intent before any work begins. Production note: this episode was recorded before the Internet of Cognition software shipped, so a few names changed between recording and release. OXP is now SCOPE — System for Cognitive Observability, Provenance & Explainability. ACCORD and CONCORD are the protocol names, not acronyms (Vijoy calls them acronyms in the episode). All three: github.com/ioc-project

items.title: Why AI Is Running on the Wrong Kind of Computer (with Vijoy Pandey)
items.summary: In Episode #1041, Dr. Vijoy Pandey (SVP and General Manager of Outshift, Cisco's incubation engine) returns for a third visit to explain why multi-agent systems fail without anyone noticing. Agents from different vendors, clouds and organisations can now exchange perfectly valid messages, but connection is not cognition: they do not agree on what those messages mean. Vijoy's team analyzed multi-agent sessions from its own production deployments and from public traces, and found a cognitive failure in every single one. In this episode, he lays out the kinds of failure he sees and how fast they compound, introduces the open-source observability platform and protocols Outshift has shipped to catch and correct drift mid-task, details a record-breaking quantum network running on real New York City fiber, and explains why probabilistic AI software running on deterministic hardware is a mismatch worth fixing. Additional materials: https://www.superdatascience.com/1041

items.title: Indian Startup Alteon Is Building Aircraft That Can Fly for Hundreds of Days
items.summary: Alteon is building autonomous aircraft that use dynamic soaring to stay airborne for months at a time. Founder Samay Sanghvi explains the albatross-inspired technology, ocean surveillance plans and India's aerospace startup push. In this exclusive Front Page interview, Mohit Pandey, Senior Tech Journalist at AIM, speaks with Samay Sanghvi, Founder and CEO of Alteon, the Bengaluru aerospace startup that recently raised about $2.5M in pre-seed funding from Lachy Groom and Together Fund. Watch to learn how dynamic soaring works, what the team learned from offshore flight tests, why the open ocean matters, how autonomous aircraft could support maritime surveillance, and what regulation, talent and timelines look like.
